title: New Jersey police mistakenly arrest man for drunk driving; he dies of heart attack in custody
text: New Jersey police mistakenly arrest man for drunk driving; he dies of heart attack in custody New Jersey police officers Lorenzo Orsi and Lucfred Petion incorrectly detained Juan Restrepo, 73, for drunk driving after a report of an intoxicated man. The footage showed that Restrepo was visibly struggling with a medical condition-likely diabetes or heart disease-as he was screaming in pain and collapsed while being handcuffed. Despite his clear need for medical assistance, the officers dismissed his distress, leading to his death in police custody. The incident highlights the importance of proper medical assessment and training in law enforcement for individuals with apparent health issues. New Jersey police mistakenly arrested a man for drunk driving, despite multiple signs that he was suffering from a health condition and required immediate medical attention. He died in police custody from a heart attack brought on by his diabetes, NJ.com reported. In June 2020, Juan Restrepo, 73, was approached by officers Lorenzo Orsi and Lucfred Petion of the Newark Police Department (NPD) after they received a report of an 'intoxicated man behind the wheel of a car,' according to New Jersey's Office of the Attorney General (NJOAG).Restrepo was sitting in the front seat of a rental car with a busted hood and deployed airbags, according to NJ.com. Restrepo was taken into custody and transported to Newark Penn Station where New Jersey Transit police attempted to breathalyze him but failed to obtain a reading. Restrepo was screaming in pain and was carried through Penn Station by police by his arms and legs as he was unable to walk, according to body camera footage cited by NJ.com.Restrepo Collapses at Police StationOfficers arrested Restrepo for his inability to take the breathalyzer test. While attempting to walk over to the police car to be taken to Newark PD's 5th Precinct to be processed, Restrepo collapsed and lay on the ground handcuffed and in pain unable to get up, according to bodycam footage seen by NJ Advance Media.Restrepo's cause of death was determined to be atherosclerotic and hypertensive cardiovascular disease Officers neglected Restrepo's screams of pain and told him to 'stop playing around' Juan Restrepo, 73, was a beloved community member and is fondly remembered by the leaders and members of Christ Church in Summit, New Jersey, where he served as a sexton for 20 years Read More Nicole Virzi is accused of the most heinous child killing. Now, read her shocking 'confession' 'C'mon Juan, stop playing around,' one officer can be heard saying.'It's like dead weight,' said another. By the time his wife, Rocio Restrepo, arrived to the hospital, he was already dead. Restrepo's cause of death was determined to be atherosclerotic and hypertensive cardiovascular disease. He was pronounced dead at 1.17pm, a little under four hours after he was initially arrested, according to NJOAG.Family Sues Newark Police DepartmentRocio Restrepo hired attorneys Scott Gorman and Stewart Leviss to look into her husband's death. Gorman was able to obtain the police body camera footage, and Leviss filed a civil lawsuit in state Superior Court, according to NJ.com. Earlier this year, Newark agreed to pay $1.75million and NJ Transit $750,000 to Rocio Restrepo, the outlet reported.'The officers' deliberate indifference to Mr. Restrepo's deteriorating medical condition as they held him under arrest for more than two hours… prevented Mr. Restrepo from getting the care which would have saved his life,' Leviss said in a statement, according to NJ.com. ' the first indication from any source that Mr. Restrepo's condition deteriorated over the course of several hours in a manner that was so obvious that a lay person would easily recognize the need for a doctor's attention,' the attorneys said.Juan Restrepo was a beloved community member and is fondly remembered by the leaders and members of Christ Church in Summit, New Jersey, where he served as a sexton for 20 years. A memorial was held at the church in Restrepo's honor the month he died, during which church members recalled countless fond memories of him.
summary: The footage showed that Restrepo was visibly struggling with a medical condition-likely diabetes or heart disease-as he was screaming in pain and collapsed while being handcuffed. New Jersey police mistakenly arrested a man for drunk driving, despite multiple signs that he was suffering from a health condition and required immediate medical attention. Restrepo was taken into custody and transported to Newark Penn Station where New Jersey Transit police attempted to breathalyze him but failed to obtain a reading.
